CtxAnswerLedger.description:
The ctx-answer ledger (LLP 0051 D1): the ordered answers the deterministic
ctx surface gave during one invocation. Record mode produces it; replay
mode consumes it. Reads are never ledgered — `ctx.db` reads always
re-evaluate against the executing tier's current view; the ledger pins
*answers* only. This is LLP 0043 M2's captured replay environment as a
defined channel: LLP 0008 pins the client wire to exactly
`{generatedIds, now}`; the auth fingerprint is server-retained and never
crosses the client wire.

auth_fingerprint.description:
Fingerprint of the resolved auth context the handler observed
(LLP 0043 §Auth posture). Checked at replay when present: a mismatch
surfaces `SNAPBACK_AUTH_STALE_RESULT` rather than replaying under new
authority. Server-retained (D1 wire split) — record-mode outputs leave
it unset on client-bound surfaces.

ids.description:
Every host-generated id, in answer order (LLP 0008's `generatedIds`):
`ctx.runtime.id()` answers and `ctx.db.insert` row-id generation share
one ordered sequence.

now.description: The frozen invocation clock every `ctx.runtime.now()` answered with.

version.description:
Ledger format version, versioned alongside the shared data-tier
profile (LLP 0051 D5) so pre-extension ledgers stay replayable.

Receipt.description:
A retention-ring receipt (LLP 0034 §3.2): connectionless facts about
mutations and subscription lifecycle, served by the receipts snapshot and
echoed in live-subscribe/unsubscribe outputs. Privacy (§3.3): receipts
carry opaque ids, versions, table names, and reasons — never row data or
argument values.

oneOf.description:
One mutation invocation: confirmed or rejected, with the write
surface that fan-out used.

affectedTables.description:
`null` means EXPLICITLY unknown (an IbexModule handler without a
declared write set) — distinct from `[]`, no tables.

rollbackReason.description:
The diagnostic CODE only — messages may embed argument values
(§3.3 privacy). `null` on confirmed mutations.

snapshotVersion.description:
`null` only when the rejected invocation could not safely read the
durable cursor; never fabricate zero from a storage failure.

oneOf.description:
Subscription lifecycle: established / disposed, on both the durable
live-query lane and the ephemeral room lane (`lane: "ephemeral"`,
which carries `bindingId`/`collection` instead of `subscriptionId`).

snapshotVersion.description:
`null` when no storage read is safe at the emission site (the
disconnect teardown path) — the honest "unknown at death" value.

description:
Successful `POST /mutation/{name}` response. The mutation output and its
terminal receipt are one closed, typed envelope; rejected mutations keep
using [`ErrorResponse`] with the same receipt attached by the error path.

@ref LLP 0051#d4-finish-dk-7-the-live-envelope-becomes-schema-governed — direct
  mutation results are part of the generated client-visible wire.
title: MutationResponse
